name: StateSet Sandbox

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: CPU basis not explicitly documented; alloc is a conservative modeling assumption, not a verified metering claim. Rates per sandbox.stateset.app/pricing (2026-09-28): Hobby/Pro overage $0.128/vCPU-h, $0.0106/GB-h (homepage rounds to $0.011), $0.15/GB network, $0.60/million creates. Team plan overage is lower ($0.10 / $0.008 / $0.12 / $0.50) but is not modelled as a separate regime (the engine would pick the cheaper Team rates before weighing the $299 fee).

modes.label: Team overage
modes.note: Team-only lower overage rates; billing granularity and allocation-vs-observed CPU wording remain unpublished.

storage.artifacts: Persistent files outside a sandbox, transferable between sandboxes, with signed time-limited download URLs; no storage price or retention limit is published.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Free. 10 concurrent sandboxes, 45-minute max runtime. Allowances are per-resource buckets (not fungible), so included_usd 0.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $49/mo. 2,000 concurrent, 5-hour max runtime. Allowances per-resource (not fungible), included_usd 0.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $299/mo. 10,000 concurrent, 5-hour max runtime. Lower overage rates ($0.10/vCPU-h, $0.008/GB-h, $0.12/GB, $0.50/M creates) not modelled; allowances per-resource, included_usd 0.

caveats: Public homepage lists compute/network/create meters. gVisor Kubernetes pods, non-root. Free CPU-hours cannot be applied to RAM or network. Runtime price shown as CPU-hour; allocated versus observed CPU metering is not fully specified.

ENGINE_CARD cannot apply all independent free CPU/RAM/storage/request allowances exactly. Raw regimes/worked example retain them; any engine subtotal may overstate charges or miss eligibility. Do not subtract them twice.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Plans re-checked 2026-09-28 on sandbox.stateset.app/pricing: Hobby $0 (10 concurrent, 45 min max), Pro $49 (2,000 concurrent, 5 h), Team $299 (10,000 concurrent, 5 h). Included vCPU-h / GB-h / network / creates are separate buckets kept as extra plan keys; the engine only understands a fungible included_usd, so they are not credited (small overstatement).

Disk: no per-sandbox disk size or disk price on the pricing page; disk beyond 0 GiB stays unknown. Snapshots: checkpoints are filesystem + env only ("Process state is not captured"), max 10 GB, retained 90 days, stored in GCS/S3; no checkpoint storage price published (snapshot_gib_month null). The docs production guide carries an older conflicting table ($0.05/vCPU-h, $0.02/GB-h, $0.20/GB-month storage, different plan limits) that is not used.

Access is API/SDK only (run commands, files, artifacts); docs mention no SSH, browser, desktop/VNC or computer-use offering, so those are set false. Pods run non-root with a read-only root filesystem (root false).

Nested virtualization set to no: every sandbox runs under gVisor, which gives the workload its own user-space kernel and no /dev/kvm device (no KVM-based emulators or VMs inside). Docker inside is a separate question.

fleet.notes: Current pricing differs from a legacy production-guide table (Free 2). Use current pricing but confirm account limits. vCPU allocation rates 40/10min Hobby, 200/min Pro, 1,000/min Team are ramp limits, not aggregate CPU quota. 50/300/1,000 fit Pro concurrency.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When a sandbox nears expiry the platform checkpoints it, creates a fresh sandbox, and restores state — seamlessly.
snapshot_auto.note: Only for Agent Sessions (sandbox rotation before timeout, pre_rotate_buffer_seconds). Filesystem + env only: checkpoints guide says 'Process state is not captured (only filesystem)'. Plain sandboxes auto-terminate at timeout without a checkpoint.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: They capture the filesystem, environment variables, and metadata at a point in time
snapshot_on_demand.note: POST /sandbox/:id/checkpoints, restore (same or a different new sandbox), clone, compare; SDK also has forkSandbox. No memory ('Process state is not captured (only filesystem)'); max 10 GB, retained 90 days.

harness_api.quote: High-level helper for running Claude Code agents in sandboxes.
harness_api.note: SDK AgentRunner.run({prompt, systemPrompt, allowedTools, mcpServers, maxTurns}) writes a Claude Agent SDK script into the sandbox and streams typed events (message/tool_use/tool_result/done) via onEvent; one-shot, no follow-up/resume API. Built on exec streaming; injects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as env. Only in the npm SDK README, not the docs site. Agent Sessions (docs) are exec/budget/event-log containers, not a harness driver. Claude Code CLI preinstalled.

egress_allowlist.quote: Set the egress policy for the organization
egress_allowlist.note: SDK types: EgressPolicy {mode: 'allow_all'|'allowed_domains'|'denied_domains'|'allowed_ports', allowed_domains, denied_domains, allowed_ports, enforcement 'enforce'|'log_only', failure_mode} via PUT /settings/egress, plus egress audit log (host/port/decision). Organization-wide, not per sandbox; documented only in SDK typings, not on docs pages. Docs site only says 'strict network policies'.

ingress_rules.quote: Create a tunnel for a sandbox port
ingress_rules.note: SDK createTunnel(sandboxId, {port, protocol, expires_in, public}) returns url, expires_at and optional token; per-port opt-in, expiring, public flag. SDK-only, not on docs pages. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Default isolation is gVisor Kubernetes pods, non-root, read-only root filesystem, so in-sandbox iptables/nftables is not available. SDK lists other isolation values ('container'|'gvisor'|'microvm'|'kata'|'wasm') whose availability is undocumented.

secret_proxy.quote: The controller decrypts the org's API key secret and injects it into the outbound request, so the API key never enters the sandbox.
secret_proxy.note: Inference proxy POST /sandbox/:id/inference for LLM providers only (provider + path + body), called with the StateSet API key through the control plane. General secrets are org secrets injected into the sandbox as env vars (injectSecrets ... as_env_vars: true), i.e. visible to the agent. No arbitrary-host / non-HTTP credential proxy.

image_oci.quote: Sandbox template. Determines the container image and pre-installed tools. - 'base' - 'claude-code' - 'browser' - 'rust' - 'go'
image_oci.note: Docs/SDK only expose fixed named templates (base/claude-code/browser/rust/go/...). The published TypeScript SDK types include an undocumented `image?: string` override field on create(), but it is not described on any docs/pricing page as a supported bring-your-own-OCI-image feature, so treated as not offered.

docker_inside.note: Sandboxes run as non-root, read-only-root-filesystem gVisor Kubernetes pods; no docs mention a container runtime (Docker/Podman) available inside the sandbox. SDK isolation enum also lists 'microvm'/'kata' but these aren't documented as running nested Docker.

anti_bot.quote: Run agent workflows in isolated Kubernetes environments. Execute code, read and write files, and store artifacts — all securely.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — this is a code-execution/agent sandbox product, not a scraping/browser-stealth product; no anti-bot or fingerprinting feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Run agent workflows in isolated Kubernetes environments. Execute code, read and write files, and store artifacts — all securely.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented anywhere on the site, docs, or SDK.

egress_ip_type.quote: gVisor runtime, non-root containers, and strict network policies.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: sandboxes are multi-tenant Kubernetes pods with shared cluster egress; no static, residential, or mobile egress IP is documented, so outbound traffic is ordinary shared datacenter IP space.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Process state is not captured (only filesystem)
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Checkpoints/forks (forkSandbox, promoteSandbox) are built on filesystem+env checkpoints only; running processes are not restored, so forks do not carry memory state.

pause_resume.quote: Pausing stops the rotation timer but keeps the sandbox running. The session can be resumed later.
pause_resume.note: pauseAgentSession/resumeAgentSession only pause the Agent Session's rotation/budget logic; the underlying sandbox keeps running (and billing) the whole time, so there is no true pause of the machine itself.

wake_on_request.quote: Each sandbox has a timeout (default and plan-based). You can set a custom timeout per sandbox within your plan limits.
wake_on_request.note: Sandboxes are created via explicit API call and auto-terminate at a fixed timeout; no docs describe a stopped/sleeping sandbox being woken automatically by an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: Persistent workspaces use a sandbox-scoped Kubernetes PVC and can participate in CSI snapshot branching when enabled.
persistent_disk.note: CreateSandboxOptions.workspace.persistence can be 'ephemeral' or 'persistent'; persistent mode backs the /workspace directory with a real PVC rather than pod-local storage. Not documented on the public docs pages, only in the SDK's TypeScript types.

volume_attach.note: Only a single per-sandbox workspace volume is exposed in the API/SDK; there is no separate API to attach additional named persistent volumes to a running sandbox.

volume_shared.quote: Persistent workspaces use a sandbox-scoped Kubernetes PVC
volume_shared.note: The workspace PVC is explicitly sandbox-scoped (one PVC per sandbox), not shareable/mountable by multiple concurrently running sandboxes.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Limits Max runtime: 45 minutes Max concurrent sandboxes: 10
auto_stop_idle.note: Sandboxes stop on a fixed max-runtime timeout set at creation, not on idle-activity detection; no idle-based auto-stop is documented.

live_resize.quote: extend(sandboxId, additionalSeconds) — Extend a sandbox lifetime by additional seconds
live_resize.note: The SDK exposes an API to extend a sandbox's remaining lifetime, but no API to change a running sandbox's CPU/memory allocation without recreating it.

own_agent_api.quote: Run agent workflows in isolated Kubernetes environments. Execute code, read and write files, and store artifacts — all securely.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — StateSet Sandbox's own first-party API drives coding-harness workflows (Claude Code via AgentRunner) and preinstalls a domain-specific `stateset` commerce CLI, but there is no first-party API for a browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: startMCPServer(sandboxId, config): Promise<{ name, pid, port, status }>
mcp_server.note: The SDK's MCP feature lets a caller start/stop/list arbitrary MCP servers running as processes inside a sandbox (the opposite direction). A separate 'stateset-mcp-server' GitHub repo is an MCP server for StateSet's e-commerce API (orders/inventory/customers), unrelated to controlling this sandbox product. No MCP server is shipped to control the sandbox platform itself.

public_ipv4.quote: pod_ip?: string — Pod IP address for direct connections.
public_ipv4.note: Sandboxes only expose an internal Kubernetes pod IP; there is no documented dedicated/public IPv4 address per sandbox. Inbound access is via HTTPS tunnels instead.

inbound_https.quote: Create a tunnel for a sandbox port
inbound_https.note: createTunnel(sandboxId, {port, protocol: 'http'|'https', expires_in, public}) returns a URL to reach a sandbox port over HTTP/HTTPS; SDK-only, not documented on the public docs pages.

egress_http_rules.note: Egress control granularity is at the domain/port level (allowed_domains, denied_domains, allowed_ports), not at the HTTP method/path level.

static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP is documented anywhere; egress goes through shared multi-tenant cluster networking with org-wide allow/deny policies, not a dedicated egress IP.

gpu.quote: Usage rates Simple metering across compute, memory, network, and creations. CPU $0.128 per vCPU-hour Memory $0.0106 per GB-hour Network $0.15 per GB Creations $0.60 per 1M
gpu.note: Pricing page meters CPU/memory/network/creates only; no GPU tier or price is published. The SDK's TypeScript types include an unused/undocumented `gpu?: GpuRequest` field on create(), but it is not marketed, priced, or documented as an available option.

windows.quote: Desktop OS (linux, windows, macos). Only linux is currently supported.
windows.note: SDK typings explicitly state only Linux is currently supported for desktop_os.

macos.quote: Desktop OS (linux, windows, macos). Only linux is currently supported.
macos.note: Same field as windows: macOS is a listed enum value but explicitly not currently supported.

arm64.quote: StateSet Sandbox is a secure, isolated execution environment for running code on behalf of AI agents. It provides containerized sandboxes with full lifecycle management, checkpointing, artifact storage, and usage tracking.
arm64.note: not offered: outside documented scope — no architecture selection or ARM machine type is mentioned anywhere in the docs, pricing, or SDK.

byoc.quote: Self-hosted Bring it to your cluster Deploy the controller on your Kubernetes cluster to control networking and data.
byoc.note: This is customer-run self-hosting (self_host=true), where the customer deploys and operates the controller themselves — not a StateSet-managed service deployed and operated inside the customer's own cloud account (BYOC).

open_source.note: The sandbox controller/product source repo (stateset/stateset-sandbox, the SDK's declared 'repository') is not publicly accessible via the GitHub API. The npm client SDK is MIT-licensed, but that is only a thin API client, not the core sandbox product, so the core product is treated as not open source.

hipaa.note: not offered: outside documented scope — only SOC 2 Type II is claimed; no HIPAA/BAA mention appears anywhere on the marketing site, docs, FAQ, or pricing pages.

eu_data_residency.quote: Team add-ons Private networking and custom VPC peering SSO/SAML and advanced audit logs Dedicated support and SLAs
eu_data_residency.note: No regions or EU data-residency option is published anywhere (card's fleet.regions is empty); the Team add-ons list covers VPC peering/SSO/audit logs but not region choice.

max_session_h.quote: Pro ... Limits Max runtime: 5 hours ... Team ... Limits Max runtime: 5 hours
max_session_h.note: Hobby plan max runtime is 45 minutes (0.75h); Pro and Team both cap at 5 hours, which is the longest available across any plan. No 'none'/unlimited option exists — every sandbox has a fixed timeout.

fork_running.quote: Checkpoints allow you to save and restore sandbox state. They capture the filesystem, environment variables, and metadata at a point in time, enabling you to: Save work in progress / Restore a sandbox to a known good state / Clone sandbox configurations for new runs
fork_running.note: The full endpoint list (production-guide) only exposes POST /sandbox/:id/checkpoints (create), POST /sandbox/:id/checkpoints/restore (restore into that same sandbox), and POST /checkpoints/:id/clone (duplicate the checkpoint record). There is no endpoint that forks/duplicates a *running* sandbox instantly — all forking/cloning goes through a saved checkpoint first, then a restore into a sandbox. This matches the card's fork:true (checkpoint-based) / fork_running:false split, but no page states 'no live fork' explicitly, so medium confidence.

nested_virt.quote: Every sandbox runs in complete isolation with gVisor, non-root containers, and strict network policies.
nested_virt.note: Isolation is gVisor-sandboxed Kubernetes pods (also stated in production-guide: 'Sandboxes	Kubernetes Pods	Isolated execution' and 'Read-only root filesystem' / 'Non-root user execution'). gVisor intercepts syscalls in userspace and does not expose /dev/kvm or hardware virtualization to the guest, so KVM-based nested VMs are not possible. No page explicitly says 'no nested virtualization', hence medium confidence rather than a direct quote settling it.

root.quote:
Read-only root filesystem
Non-root user execution
root.note: Production guide's Security > Sandbox Isolation section explicitly lists non-root execution and a read-only root filesystem as security properties of every sandbox pod; homepage repeats 'Non-root container execution'.

ssh.quote:
Method	Endpoint	Description
POST	/api/v1/sandbox/create	Create sandbox
GET	/api/v1/sandbox/:id	Get sandbox details
GET	/api/v1/sandbox/:id/status	Get sandbox status (lightweight)
POST	/api/v1/sandbox/:id/execute	Execute command
POST	/api/v1/sandbox/:id/files	Write files
GET	/api/v1/sandbox/:id/files?path=...	Read file
POST	/api/v1/sandbox/:id/stop	Stop sandbox
DELETE	/api/v1/sandbox/:id	Delete sandbox
GET	/api/v1/sandboxes	List sandboxes
ssh.note: The production guide's complete API reference (sandbox, checkpoints, artifacts, webhooks) has no SSH/terminal-access endpoint; the homepage also says 'Five endpoints. That's all you need.' (Create, Execute, Write, Read, Store) — access is exec-over-HTTP only.

desktop.quote:
Simple, powerful API

Five endpoints. That's all you need.
1 Create / 2 Execute / 3 Write / 4 Read / 5 Store
desktop.note: The full API reference in the production guide (sandbox, checkpoints, artifacts, webhooks endpoints) contains no VNC/remote-desktop/GUI endpoint or dashboard feature for viewing a sandbox desktop; product is headless code-execution only.

browser.quote:
Simple, powerful API

Five endpoints. That's all you need.
1 Create / 2 Execute / 3 Write / 4 Read / 5 Store
browser.note: No browser-automation/Chromium-in-sandbox endpoint anywhere in the docs (production-guide's full endpoint list covers sandbox/checkpoints/artifacts/webhooks only); the only 'browser' mention on the site is 'useful for browser downloads' about signed artifact URLs opened in the user's own local browser, unrelated to an in-sandbox browser feature.

computer_use.quote:
Simple, powerful API

Five endpoints. That's all you need.
1 Create / 2 Execute / 3 Write / 4 Read / 5 Store
computer_use.note: No computer-use / GUI-control tool or API is mentioned anywhere in docs; the product's own agent tooling (AgentRunner / Claude Code CLI) is limited to shell exec + file I/O, consistent with the exec-only 'five endpoints' positioning.

usage_api.quote: API Endpoints: Registration & API Keys, Sandboxes, Checkpoints, Artifacts, Webhooks. Dashboard pages include Usage (/dashboard/usage) for viewing usage and billing. No GET /api/v1/usage or billing endpoint listed.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; StateSet Sandbox tracks usage (usage_events in database) and exposes it via the /dashboard/usage web page, but does not provide a programmatic API to retrieve usage metrics or cost per sandbox or by tag. Usage is accessible only through the UI dashboard or billing invoices.
